Rogaela State: Twenty-three first-place votes for a team that lost in the quarterfinals, and the explanation is on the roster rather than in the record. Nine Valiants went in the draft — four of them in the first round, headed by Ryskamp winner Gudrun Rosenwetter at fifth overall — and the voters still see the deepest two-deep in Jyras Bay: Itsuki Nagamaki is the best returning receiver in the conference, Hwanki Kurobashi is a senior corner, and five-star tailback Maisie Althauer arrives as the jewel of a six-blue-chip class. Rami Campbell starts year fourteen with two new coordinators, one of them Anaru Manutai, pried loose from Ranroman State. A 9-0 conference run last year gives way to a schedule that doesn't see Will Tech until week 13.
Eastern State: The champions scored 49 in Stamford and then lost the man who built it: Tage Ludendorf left for Pistolheart, and two starters in the secondary followed him out the door. Bhaskar El-Mahdi, Roosevelt's offensive coordinator, inherits a title-game offense almost intact — Boubacar Grimaldi is back at quarterback, and only two Eagles were drafted. Twenty-four first-place votes, the most in the poll, with the second-most points. The week-3 date with Yrei Trobniy and the week-6 trip to Ciarralotta Tech will say early whether a new voice changes the sound.
Central Stanton: A 13-2 year ended in the Steam Bowl against Crayellan, and the offseason took seven players to the draft and defensive coordinator Gwen Oberoi to the Leafette job. What's left is still the fourth-hardest schedule in the country and a program that has been 1 or 2 in the preseason three years running. Heriberto Campovieja carries the ball, Shengli Hoshimura holds the secondary, and five-star tackle Ximena Coldcombe starts as a freshman. Boris Walker's seventh year runs through Kaji Daun on the road in week 5 and Eona at home in week 8.
Kaji Daun: The hardest schedule in the country, and the voters still have it fourth. Last year's 12-3 ended at home against Will Tech in the quarterfinals; the draft took seven, but only one in the first round. Ruolan Xuegang and Alofa Kickinghorn anchor a veteran line, Ravonei Veslovei is a senior corner, and five-star Zlata Radushkin joins Lucia Pellatelli in the backfield. Fatima Larsen's fifth year opens with Eona in week 2 and Central Stanton in week 5; the Kaji Kita finish in week 14 closes a six-game stretch against ranked teams.
Crayellan: The national runner-up loses almost nothing it chose to keep: two draft picks, and offensive coordinator Kadhim Nagarajan to Ciarralotta Tech. What it lost it lost to the portal — five transfers out, including a starting corner to Crayellan State and a linebacker to UN Steelbridge. The December run (Tengus State, Orlot in overtime, Central Stanton, Hatesei) was built on the defensive line, and Finn Milkov and Mamadou Gangalingam are both back. Five-star linebacker Kiara Woolbridge heads a small, blue-chip-heavy class of eleven. The Mountain Valley gauntlet comes late: Verigon, Fiota Bay, Costique River, Crayellan State in the last seven weeks.
Eona: Sixth in the poll at 7-5, which is the pedigree vote: this is a 2038 champion that started last season in the top ten and finished out of the playoff. The two-deep is young — three of the five headline players are sophomores — and eight Eona players were drafted, though Ustevaw Quisniy was the only first-rounder. Hollis Upshaw's third year has the fifth-hardest schedule, with Kaji Daun in week 2 and the North Hatesei trip in week 3 before September is out.
North Hatesei: Seventh at 7-5 with a 4-5 conference record, and a new coordinator on both sides of the ball. The vote is for the name — three titles between 2024 and 2030 — and for a receiving corps that returns Terrell Highcombe and Rowena Vieuxpierre as juniors. Three were drafted, none in the first round; Itsuki Tingrui comes in from San Diego Valley to help a secondary that gave up a safety to the portal. The ninth-hardest schedule puts Eona at home in week 3 and Kaji Daun at home in week 9.
Tengus State: Layla Smith's thirteenth year starts with four returning headliners on a defense that sent Bhaskar Ramasekaran to the first round. Last year's 9-5 ended in the first round against Crayellan, 25-20, which the voters have decided was a coin flip. Four transfers in, none out; five-star corner Tamsin Kirchdorf tops a class of thirteen. The Power North title goes through Skeenerland State in week 12 and the Tengus trip in week 14, and the week-0 opener against Barhold State is the league's first game.
Eternal Fox: Fourteen wins, a perfect East Forest run, a No. 3 seed, and a quarterfinal in the Redwood Bowl that ended 30-10 the wrong way. The voters' response is ninth — the only non-Power team in the top 25 — and five first-place votes from people who think the Fox were the best team nobody played. Tomavaw Norrevei went third overall in the draft, and offensive coordinator Dante Valloncelli left to run Sacred Tomb. Chumani Grayelk and Aoi Tae-Hwan hold the linebacking corps; five-star tackle Tamsin Stoneford is the biggest recruit in school history. Fiota Bay at home in week 7 is the one Power game on the 148th-ranked schedule.
Ranroman State: A 6-6 team with a 3-6 conference record ranked tenth is a statement about who's on the roster, and that is Litowa Mesteniy's point: eight players were drafted and the two-deep still has six juniors and a sophomore end in Omar Geortellis at the top of it. Defensive coordinator Anaru Manutai left for Rogaela State. The fifteenth-hardest schedule puts North Hatesei, Crayellan, Central Stanton and Eona on the home slate.
Skeenerland State: The voters' fifth-best team on paper and eleventh in the poll, which is what a 34-13 first-round loss to Holliday does to a reputation. Nine Skeeners were drafted, Isamu Yamasato seventh overall. The remaining defense is young and expensive — Ngaio Malieanua is a sophomore end and five-star Sachiko Qinzei joins him as a freshman — and Abiodun El-Ghazali is a junior quarterback with a full year of starts. Ji-woo Hall, in year eleven, has never won a title here. Tengus State on the road in week 12 and Kaji Kita at home in week 13 decide the Power North.
Park Island: An 8-1 Western Coast champion at 11-3, with the longest-tenured coordinator pair in the top 25: Lagi Naeata in his ninth year running the defense, Hosei Joroviy in his sixth with the offense. Shreya Somarajan left early and went 21st. Norbert Ackerwetter and Solveig Forsnes are back at linebacker, Wei Littlesky is a senior kicker, and five-star receiver Masaru Wakamaki is the headline of a six-blue-chip class. Roosevelt in week 4 and Yrei Trobniy at home in week 9 are the conference's two games of consequence.
Hatesei: A semifinalist at 11-4 that beat Rogaela State in the 501 Bowl before Crayellan ended it in Billiataho. Two first-round picks gone, Darnell Whitbrook early. Oksana Fuentevieja and Koharu Baizhen are seniors at corner and tackle, and five-star safety Wenbo Shanjian starts the pipeline behind them. Siegfried Oberg arrives from Hoganelle to compete at quarterback. The sixth-hardest schedule: Orlot in week 3, Central Stanton on the road in week 9, Kaji Daun at home in week 12, North Hatesei to finish.
Ciarralotta Tech: Ten wins and a second-round exit in a year that produced Sunita Lozano in the first round and six others in later ones. Uili Tendulkar pulled Kadhim Nagarajan from the national runner-up to run the offense, and the portal brought four in, including tight end Bronislaw Haselwetter from Vaughn Bay State. Maelys Lundvoll is a senior linebacker on a roster otherwise built on juniors. Eastern State comes to town in week 6, the Broad South's first real measure of the post-Ludendorf champions.
Orlot: Bertram Lorrovei was the first pick in the draft and Mariana Valmayor went ninth; that's a 10-3 team's two best players gone in a week. The overtime loss to Crayellan in the second round, 18-16, was the margin between a quarterfinal and this. Kalani Almeida's eighth year has two sophomore quarterbacks competing (Milagros Fiorini and junior Tamika Nofoalofa) and five-star tight end Uili Montenueva in the class. Thirteenth-hardest schedule, with Hatesei on the road in week 3 and Eona at home in week 11.
Fiota Bay: A 7-2 Mountain Valley record and a 41-17 first-round loss at Verigon. Afamasaga Tallarrow left early for the draft; the rest of the two-deep is back, including both junior linemen. The class is the biggest of Catalina Eastwood's tenure at nineteen. The eighteenth-hardest schedule has the one non-conference game in the top 25 that nobody else wanted: Eternal Fox on the road in week 7, with Crayellan at home two weeks later.
Will Tech: A 13-4 semifinalist that won in Chapel Rock and Ediville before Eastern State stopped it 17-10 in Port Logan, and the voters have it seventeenth because the receivers are seniors and the coordinator is new. Tengfei Shiraura left to take the Dove Island State job. Annika Weinheim and Akari Xuetun are senior starters at receiver and tackle; Kirovei Noyosei is the best kicker in the Jyras Bay. Three transfers out, including a starting tailback to Clark. The conference title is decided in week 13 at Rogaela State.
Crayellan State: A 28-27 first-round loss to Canesta State, and then a busy offseason: four in through the portal (a quarterback, a kicker, two corners — one of them from Crayellan), four out, and defensive coordinator Esteban Oakmere to the Greene job. Chengfei Pyeong-Seok is a senior quarterback with Aldo Ashdale behind him from Keytommiyr. On paper this is a top-ten roster; the voters want to see it in November, when Verigon, Fiota Bay and the Crayellan trip come in four weeks.
Ranroman: The second-hardest schedule in the country for a 5-7 team with a new head coach — Ghislaine Penahermosa, poached from UN Ediville after an 8-4 year — ranked nineteenth because the voters know the name and nine draft picks say the talent was there. Urmila Jayawardhan stays as defensive coordinator for a ninth year. Tsumugi Zhenxiong and Tsuvai Peytravaw are seniors; Eunkyung Eun-Jin arrives from Crayellan at receiver. The class of twenty has only three blue-chips. Kaji Daun and Orlot come to town in weeks 6 and 7.
Verigon: Ten wins, a first-round rout of Fiota Bay, and then Hatesei 49-21. Rocio Santarini left early and went 25th. Kyungja U-Cheol is a sophomore quarterback with a year of starts; five-star tight end Percy Nishiyama starts as a freshman, and the portal brought a quarterback from Churchill to push. Four in, none out. Bhaskar Al-Adawi's third year gets Fiota Bay at home in week 2 and Crayellan at home in week 8.
Kaji Kita: Seven wins, a 6-3 conference record, and two first-round picks on the defensive line — Dieter Schwarzstein and Narendra Rifai, the latter a year early. Efua Kofbuike's twelfth year running the offense is the longest coordinator tenure in the Power North. Jayla Folasowah is the senior receiver. On paper this is one of the ten best rosters in the country, and the schedule gives it the chance to prove it late: Skeenerland State on the road in week 13 and Kaji Daun at home in week 14.
Costique River: A 9-4 year that ended in a 49-36 first-round shootout with Black Forest, and only one draft pick — a roster that returns almost whole. Lifen Tichovich is a sophomore quarterback; Milena Tichushkin, a tight end from Will Tech, joins Sylvie Blancmont for a two-tight-end offense. Three out through the portal, two of them to Underwood. The class of twenty is the biggest in the Mountain Valley. Crayellan State at home in week 9, Fiota Bay at home in week 11, Crayellan on the road in week 13.
Barhold: A 7-5 team with three titles since 1987 and a special-teams room that would start anywhere: Armand Lachamp and Ayanna Kofemeka at kicker, Tatsuya Murong at punter, plus a kicker from North Canesta through the portal. Yasmin El-Nadim is a senior tight end. Four drafted, none in the first round. Darnell Ellery's second year opens at Barhold Valley in week 0 and gets Skeenerland State at home in week 8.
Yrei Trobniy: An 8-4 team that lost defensive coordinator Cecily Rosenhauer to the UN Ediville job and a starting corner to Kaji Kita, and ranks 24th on the strength of a sophomore quarterback — Sungmin Zhenbin — and a schedule that projects to eight wins. Two draft picks. The week-3 trip to Eastern State is the Western Coast's only September game against a top-five team; Park Island on the road in week 9.
Roosevelt: Seven wins, a 4-5 conference record, and a 13-0 week-0 loss at Barhold Valley that cost the Rough Riders a preseason top-five ranking a year ago. The voters have learned: twenty-fifth, with a top-fifteen roster on paper and an 8.4-win projection, the highest of any team in the bottom ten of the poll. Offensive coordinator Bhaskar El-Mahdi left to coach the champions; both coordinators are new. Friedrich Fuafolau and Armand Lamont went in the first round a year early; Kazue Yoshigaki and Nicolas Grandmaison are the next pair. Sione Baker's eighth year has Hatesei in week 2 and Park Island in week 4, both at home.
